Question: Which pistol was replaced by a pistol manufactured by Spreewerk?
Thought 1: I need to find a pistol that was replaced by a pistol manufactured by Spreewerk. I will start by searching for "Spreewerk" to see if it mentions any pistols it manufactured and what they replaced.
Action 1: Search[Spreewerk]
Observation 1: Metallwarenfabrik Spreewerk GmbH was a German weapons manufacturing company. Spreewerk produced a number of important weapons and components before and during World War II including 280,880[1] of the Walther P.38 pistol which was the standard service pistol of the German Heer, and the famous 8.8 cm Flak anti-aircraft gun.. The Berlin-Karlsruher Industrie Werke (BERKA) was founded in 1920 as a successor to the Deutsche Waffen und Munitionsfabriken AG, one of Germany's largest munitions firms of the prewar era. Under the regime of the Versailles treaty the firm was forced to give up the manufacture of armaments, which had been its core business. Most of the facilities that had grown up to meet the needs of war were reduced and BERKA carried on with factories in Berlin and Karlsruhe, manufacturing a variety of light metal goods..
Thought 2: The text mentions that Spreewerk produced the Walther P.38 pistol, which was the standard service pistol of the German Heer. This implies it was a replacement for a previous standard service pistol. I need to find what the Walther P.38 replaced. I will search for "Walther P.38" to see if it mentions what it replaced.
Action 2: Search[Walther P.38]
Observation 2: Could not find Walther P.38. Similar: ['Walther P38', 'List of Lupin III television specials (redirect from In Memory of the Walther P-38)', 'Spreewerk', 'Tomokazu Tokoro', 'Manurhin'].
Thought 3: I should search for "Walther P38" as the previous search suggested.
Action 3: Search[Walther P38]
Observation 3: The Walther P38 (originally written Walther P.38) is a 9 mm semi-automatic pistol that was developed by Carl Walther GmbH as the service pistol of the Wehrmacht at the beginning of World War II. It was intended to replace the comparatively complex and expensive to produce Luger P08. Moving the production lines to the more easily mass producible P38 once World War II started took longer than expected, leading to the P08 remaining in production until September 1942 and copies remained in service until the end of the war.[7]. As the previous service pistol, the Luger P08, was expensive to produce, Germany started to look for a replacement as early as 1927, settling on the Walther P38 in 1938, which offered similar performance to the Luger P08 but took almost half the time to produce.[8] The first design was submitted to the German Army and featured a locked breech and a hidden hammer but the Army requested that it should be redesigned with an external hammer.[citation needed]. The P38 concept was accepted by the German military in 1938 but production of prototype ("Test") pistols did not begin until late 1939.
Thought 4: The Walther P38, manufactured by Spreewerk, replaced the Luger P08.
Action 4: Finish[Luger P08]
